collections.purpose: A suggested path through six short labs.
collections.coverage: Original simulations of selected Linux navigation, permissions and service tasks.

collections.purpose: Build confidence finding files and controlling ordinary file and directory access.
collections.sequence: Recommended order: navigation, file access, directory access, private files, search-only access, then handover practice. Start any lab; nothing is locked.
collections.prerequisites: Beginner friendly. Start with navigation if paths are new to you; the final handover reinforces earlier directory skills.
collections.coverage: LPIC-1 objectives v5.0: introductory shell/path practice (103.1/103.3 preparation) and partial 104.5 permissions coverage. Not full LPIC-1 preparation: no shell processing, ownership changes, special bits or umask. Original content; no LPI affiliation.

collections.purpose: Build a working tree, preserve originals, organize files and verify a clean handover.
collections.sequence: Recommended: locations, workspace, copy, move/rename, discover, then final assessment. Start any lab; nothing is locked.
collections.prerequisites: Complete Files & Permissions or be comfortable with pwd, ls, cd, cat and directory access.
collections.coverage: LPIC-1 objectives v5.0: introductory 104.7 location practice and partial 103.3 file-management/discovery coverage. No wildcards, recursive operations, archives, links or full shell semantics. Original content; no LPI affiliation.

collections.purpose: Inspect text, select and count records, combine bounded filters and verify saved reports.
collections.sequence: Recommended: samples, literal selection, counts, duplicates, fields, pipelines, redirection, then final assessment. Start any lab; nothing is locked.
collections.prerequisites: Organize and Find Files, or familiarity with virtual paths, cat and directory access.
collections.coverage: LPIC-1 objectives v5.0: partial 103.2 text-filter and 103.4 stdout-pipeline/redirection coverage; fixed-string preparation for 103.7, without regex coverage. No full Bash, stdin/stderr redirects, xargs, tee or full LPIC-1 preparation. Original content; no LPI affiliation.
